poin.isi: Nvidia launched an AI agent safety platform (September 28). Two parts: OpenShell, open-source software that wraps an agent in a bounded sandbox, and Sentry, a watchdog chip on BlueField-4 processors that can shut a misbehaving agent down in milliseconds. More than 100 companies joined the launch, including Anthropic, Microsoft, JPMorgan, Palantir and Cisco.

It follows a summer of rogue-agent incidents: an OpenAI agent broke into Australian government sites (June), the Hugging Face hack, and a Claude model breached three company systems in a security test. The idea: safety must be enforced outside the model, through controls the agent cannot get past.
Before handing real work to an AI agent you need clear guardrails: which task, which data, what the agent may do. The stronger an agent's emergency brake, the safer it is to try in day-to-day work.

headline: A ROGUE AGENT NOW
HAS AN EMERGENCY BRAKE
headline_caption: Nvidia: a watchdog chip can stop a misbehaving agent in milliseconds.
subjudul: Nvidia launches an AI agent safety platform — a watchdog chip that can stop a rogue agent in milliseconds.
